strategy.angle: The shift from digital chatter to operational reality in industrial AI.
strategy.audience: Houston business leaders, energy executives, and industrial operations managers.

draft.hook: Your current AI strategy is likely focused on chatbots—and that's exactly why you're missing the trillion-dollar shift happening in industrial automation.
draft.body:
The real frontier isn't writing emails; it is the transition to 'Physical AI.' NVIDIA and LG Group’s recent pivot into AI factories proves this: the future of heavy industry belongs to AI that can perceive, reason, and act within the physical world. For Houston’s business sector, this shifts the benchmark from operational efficiency to total autonomous capability in mobility and robotics. 

What does this mean for your bottom line? It means the gap between information processing and true operational automation is closing. Data suggests that companies integrating embodied AI into their supply chains expect a 20-30% reduction in logistical friction by 2027. 

How do legacy Houston firms compete against this? By treating 'Physical AI' as the new infrastructure, not a software add-on. At Amplify Intelligence, Leon Coe has been helping leadership teams identify where their operational data meets physical hardware, ensuring that these investments don't just generate insights, but drive movement and production on the ground.
draft.closing: The bottleneck for industrial growth is no longer information access; it is the integration of digital intelligence into physical output.
draft.cta: If you are still running a digital-only AI roadmap, tell me—where is your physical automation strategy breaking down?
